entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil Secrett. Lko.

And Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Manoj Kumar Dubey,Deena Nath Mishra

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
Vakalatnama filed by Sri Sridhar Awasthi, advocate, learned counsel for opposite party no. 3 is taken
on record.

Heard the learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 3, the
learned Aga for the State and perused the record.

The instant application has been filed with a prayer to quash the criminal proceedings arising out of
case no. 1317 of 2019 in case crime no. 666/2018 u/s- 498A/323/504 Ipc read with 3/4 of the
Dowry Prohibition Act, lodged at Ps Indira Nagar, District-Lucknow, pending in the court of Acjm
Ii, lucknow and to quash the chargesheet, summoning order dated 26.07.2019 in case no. 1317 of
2019 in case crime no. 666 of 2018 u/s- 498A/323/504 Ipc read with 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition
Act, lodged at Ps Indira Nagar, District-Lucknow.
The learned counsel appearing for the applicants that the present matter relates to matrimonial
dispute between the husband and wife and due to certain misunderstanding, the instant Fir was
lodged against the applicants and thereafter the parties sat together and has amicably settled their

sentences.text: dispute which has been reduced in writing on 08.12.2022

. He added that thereafter the applicants filed the instant application for direction to the trial Court to verify the compromise deed and in compliance of the order dated 02.02.2023, the verification was done and report has been submitted to this Court vide order dated 08.12.2022.
He submits that further criminal proceeding in the instant matter would amount to harassment and thus the instant criminal proceeding arising out of Case Crime No.666 of 2018 may be quashed.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no.3 has also supported the contention of the learned counsel for the applicants and submits that parties have amicable settled their dispute and the opposite party no. 3 has no grievance, hence, criminal proceedings against the applicants the applicants may be dropped.
Learned counsel for the State has no objection to the contention aforesaid.

Considering the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, I find that compromise has been entered into between the parties on 08.12.2022 and said compromise has been verified on 02.02.2023 and, now, as per the statement of learned counsel for the parties, they do not want to press the aforementioned criminal case relating to Case Crime No. 666 of 2018.

In view of the above, as the applicants and opposite parties have entered into compromise on 08.12.2022 and no grievance remains to be agitated and as such, further criminal proceedings in the aforementioned criminal case are liable to be set aside in view of the Judgements of the Apex Court rendered in B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003)4 SCC 675; Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation[2008)9 SCC 677]; Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; and Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab ( 2014) 6 SCC 466.
Accordingly, criminal proceedings arising out of case no. 1317 of 2019 in case crime no. 666/2018 u/s- 498A/323/504 IPC read with 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, lodged at PS Indira Nagar,
District-Lucknow, pending in the court of ACJM II, lucknow and to quash the chargesheet,
summoning order dated 26.07.2019 in case no. 1317 of 2019 in case crime no. 666 of 2018 u/s- 498A/323/504 IPC read with 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, lodged at PS Indira Nagar,
District-Lucknow are hereby quashed.
